Every kick in Hitech Arsenal Vol. 1 is tuned to a key. I measured them: the F# kick sits at 46.2 Hz, F at 43.7, G at 49.0, E at 41.2. Each one lands on its note.

The loops are cut to whole bars. A 200 BPM bass loop is 211,680 samples at 44.1 kHz: exactly four bars, so it locks to the grid.

In the video: Rolling, Growl and Snappy kick+bass loops, then an FM sequence in the same key on top, all straight from the pack in Ableton.

120 sounds: 12 kicks, 16 bass one-shots, 12 bass loops, 12 FM leads, 8 stabs, 25 glitch perc, 12 hats, 15 FX, 8 synth loops. 24-bit WAV, every file labelled with key and BPM, royalty-free for your own releases. 15 €, link in bio.

#codechaos #samplepack #hitech #psycore #newpsychedelicdeathart

Hinter den Kulissen: der Drop von Uhrwerk aus Blut, direkt aus meiner Ableton-Session. 104 Spuren, 210 BPM.

Auf dem Lead-Bus: Hochpass bei 150 Hz, Glue-Kompressor 2:1, Echo auf 1/8 punktiert, Dark Hall mit 2,4 s Nachhall.

Freitag, 30.10. Pre-Save über den Link in der Bio.

#codechaos #hitech #psytrance #newpsychedelicdeathart #abletonlive

This hitech snare is three sounds hitting at the same time.

Layers one and two: a 909 snare and a 909 clap in a Drum Rack, same notes on beats two and four. EQ Eight cuts them below 180 Hz and adds 2 dB at 3.2 kHz, then Shifter in ring mode at 180 Hz, 30 % wet, adds a metallic ring.

Layer three is the zap: Operator, a sine plus white noise at -8 dB. A pitch envelope drops the sine 36 semitones in 45 ms. Measured, it is 20 dB down after 23 ms. EQ Eight cuts it below 400 Hz, so the low end stays free for kick and bass.

Together: the 909 is brightest above 5 kHz, the zap fills 1 to 5 kHz.

From my new track Uhrwerk aus Blut, out 30.10. Part 5 next: the FM leads.
